gloss: to begin to move; to start moving

definitions.gloss: to begin to move; to start moving
definitions.explanation: To start physical movement after being still. Can refer to machines, vehicles, people, or animals beginning motion.

definitions.gloss: to start to take action; to get underway
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, for a project, plan, organization, or situation to begin progressing or developing.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}がゆっくりと{動|うご}き{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: The train slowly began to move.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}ちゃんが{自分|じぶん}で{動|うご}き{始|はじ}める{時期|じき}だ。
examples.english: It's the age when babies start moving on their own.

examples.japanese: {修理|しゅうり}が{終|お}わって、やっとエンジンが{動|うご}き{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: After the repair was finished, the engine finally started running.

examples.japanese: プロジェクトが{動|うご}き{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: The project started to get underway.

examples.japanese: {世論|せろん}が{動|うご}き{始|はじ}めている。
examples.english: Public opinion is starting to shift.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{法律|ほうりつ}の{施行|しこう}に{向|む}けて、{行政|ぎょうせい}が{動|うご}き{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: The government has started taking action toward implementing the new law.

notes:
A compound verb formed from {動|うご}く (to move) and {始|はじ}める (to begin). The ~{始|はじ}める auxiliary pattern is very productive in Japanese, attaching to the stem of other verbs to express the beginning of an action.

TRANSITIVITY: Intransitive

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ゆっくりと{動|うご}き{始|はじ}める: to slowly begin to move
- やっと{動|うご}き{始|はじ}める: to finally start moving
- {本格的|ほんかくてき}に{動|うご}き{始|はじ}める: to start moving in earnest

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {動|うご}き{出|だ}す: to start moving — similar meaning, more sudden or spontaneous nuance
- {始動|しどう}する: to start up — more formal, often for machines or systems
